bull.last: SOFI: argues short. SOFI just broke its 20‑day high to $16.54 on 2.45× volume, but it remains under both the 50‑day (16.63) and 200‑day (17.93) moving averages, confirming a down‑trend. The stock carries a hefty short‑interest of 16.9% of float and short sellers accounted for 49.3% of the day’s volume, indicating a large pool of sellers ready to profit on a pull‑back. Fundamentals are weak – the company is still loss‑making (‑19.8% net margin) and EPS growth is negative, while the PE of 29.4 is inflated for a fintech with no earnings. With beta at 2.29 the rally is likely to be volatile and vulnerable to a reversal, making a short‑fade of the breakout the higher‑probability trade.

bear.last: SOFI: The stock just punched through its 20‑day high of $16.25 on 2.45× volume, but that breakout is fragile because it still sits below the 50‑day SMA ($16.63) and the 200‑day SMA ($17.93), keeping the longer‑term downtrend intact. Recent earnings beat and a FY2026 guidance lift sparked a >9% rally, and the consensus analyst outlook is bullish (mean target $20.22, 22.3% upside), suggesting the market may keep buying on optimism. Short interest is already high at 16.9% of float and short sellers accounted for 49.3% of the day’s volume, creating a classic squeeze setup if the price holds above the breakout level. The options market shows a 4.96% implied move and a put‑call ratio of 0.57, both pointing to continued buying pressure, while the stock’s beta of 2.29 means any upside can be amplified. All of these factors mean the short could be caught in a rapid reversal, turning a modest pull‑back target into a steep loss.
